review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

8:1.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν ἐλαιῶν.
8:1.targetText: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:2.sourceText: Ὄρθρου δὲ πάλιν παρεγένετο εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν. καὶ καθίσας ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
8:2.targetText: Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.

groups.note: πάλιν ("again") is rendered back: He went back.
The imperfect ἐδίδασκεν ("He was teaching") is rendered to teach.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

8:3.sourceText: ἄγουσι δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς αὐτὸν γυναῖκα ἐν μοιχείᾳ κατειλημμένην, καὶ στήσαντες αὐτὴν ἐν μέσῳ,
8:3.targetText: The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them

groups.note: Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
BSB's Greek has a different preposition with the same meaning here.
ἐν μέσῳ ("in the middle") is rendered before them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

8:4.sourceText: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ, Διδάσκαλε, αὕτη ἡ γυνὴ κατελήφθη ἐπαυτοφώρῳ μοιχευομένη.
8:4.targetText: and said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.

groups.note: Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text.
ἐπαυτοφώρῳ ("in the very act") is spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The participle μοιχευομένη ("committing adultery") is rendered of adultery.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle στήσαντες of verse 3 to the main verb.

8:5.sourceText: ἐν δὲ τῷ νόμῳ Μωσῆς ἡμῖν ἐνετείλατο τὰς τοιαύτας λιθοβολεῖσθαι· σὺ οὖν τί λέγεις;
8:5.targetText: In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?”

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
τὰς τοιαύτας ("such women") is rendered such a woman.
The passive "to be stoned" is rendered active; BSB's Greek has another verb with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

8:6.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγον πειράζοντες αὐτόν, ἵνα ἔχωσι κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κάτω κύψας, τῷ δακτύλῳ ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν·
8:6.targetText: They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.

groups.note: The participle πειράζοντες ("testing") is rendered as purpose, to test.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The article serves as a possessive: His finger.
The imperfect is rendered began to write; BSB's Greek has another form of this verb with the same meaning.

The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

8:7.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐπέμενον ἐρωτῶντες αὐτόν, ἀνάκυψας εἶπε πρὸς αὐτοὺς, Ὁ ἀναμάρτητος ὑμῶν πρῶτος τὸν λίθον ἐπ’ αὐτῇ βαλέτω.
8:7.targetText: When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.”

groups.note: BSB's Greek has another form of this verb with the same meaning.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
BSB's Greek expresses to them in another form with the same meaning.

8:8.sourceText: καὶ πάλιν κάτω κύψας ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν.
8:8.targetText: And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has another form of this verb with the same meaning.

8:9.sourceText: οἱ δὲ, ἀκούσαντες καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς συνειδήσεως ἐλεγχόμενοι, ἐξήρχοντο εἷς καθεῖς, ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἕως τῶν ἐσχάτων· καὶ κατελείφθη μόνος ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἐν μέσῳ ἑστῶσα.
8:9.targetText: When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.

groups.note: In οἱ δέ the article serves as the pronoun they.
The imperfect ἐξήρχοντο is rendered began to go away.
Same expression, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
καί ("and") is rendered with: with the woman standing there.
ἐν μέσῳ ("in the middle") is rendered there.
BSB's Greek has a different participle here; standing renders this one.

BSB follows a reading without these words ("and convicted by their conscience").
BSB does not render τῶν ἐσχάτων ("the last ones") separately; until … only Jesus was left carries the sense.
BSB joins this clause with until instead of rendering καί.

8:10.sourceText: ἀνακύψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ μηδένα θεασάμενος πλὴν τῆς γυναικὸς, εἶπεν αὐτῇ, Ἡ γυνὴ, ποῦ εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι οἱ κατήγοροί σου; οὐδείς σε κατέκρινεν;
8:10.targetText: Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?”

groups.note: Ἡ γυνή, a nominative used in address, is rendered Woman; BSB's Greek has another form of this word.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB follows a reading without these words ("and seeing no one but the woman").
ἐκεῖνοι ("those") has no counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:11.sourceText: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν, Οὐδείς, κύριε. εἶπε δὲ αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, Οὐδὲ ἐγώ σε κατακρίνω· πορεύου καὶ μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε.)
8:11.targetText: “No one, Lord,” she answered.  “Then neither do I condemn you,” Jesus declared. “Now go and sin no more.”

groups.note: In ἡ δέ the article serves as the pronoun she.
Same verb, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῇ ("to her") unexpressed.

BSB follows a reading with extra words here, rendered Now; N1904 lacks them.

8:12.sourceText: Πάλιν οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου· ὁ ἀκολουθῶν μοι οὐ μὴ περιπατήσῃ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, ἀλλ’ ἕξει τὸ φῶς τῆς ζωῆς.
8:12.targetText: Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

groups.note: αὐτοῖς ("to them") is rendered to the people.
Same pronoun, in another form in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:13.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι Σὺ περὶ σεαυτοῦ μαρτυρεῖς· ἡ μαρτυρία σου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής.
8:13.targetText: So the Pharisees said to Him, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.”

groups.note: ἀληθής ("true") is rendered valid, of testimony.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:14.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Κἂν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία μου, ὅτι οἶδα πόθεν ἦλθον καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγω· ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἔρχομαι ἢ ποῦ ὑπάγω.
8:14.targetText: Jesus replied, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.
The present ἔρχομαι ("I come") is rendered came.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:15.sourceText: ὑμεῖς κατὰ τὴν σάρκα κρίνετε, ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω οὐδένα.
8:15.targetText: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.

groups.note: The double negative οὐ … οὐδένα is rendered no one.

8:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν κρίνω δὲ ἐγώ, ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ ἀληθινή ἐστιν, ὅτι μόνος οὐκ εἰμί, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πέμψας με.
8:16.targetText: But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered with: I am with the Father.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB uses a semicolon instead of rendering ἀλλά.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πέμψας με ("but I and the One who sent Me") has none.
BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered Father.

8:17.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ δὲ τῷ ὑμετέρῳ γέγραπται ὅτι δύο ἀνθρώπων ἡ μαρτυρία ἀληθής ἐστιν.
8:17.targetText: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.

groups.note: The possessive adjective ὑμετέρῳ is emphatic: your own.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

8:18.sourceText: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, καὶ μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὁ πέμψας με Πατήρ.
8:18.targetText: I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds also; the Greek has only the one καί, rendered and.

8:19.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Πατήρ σου; ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὔτε ἐμὲ οἴδατε οὔτε τὸν Πατέρα μου· εἰ ἐμὲ ᾔδειτε, καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου ἂν ᾔδειτε.
8:19.targetText: “Where is Your Father?” they asked Him.  “You do not know Me or My Father,” Jesus answered. “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:20.sourceText: Ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα ἐλάλησεν ἐν τῷ γαζοφυλακίῳ διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπίασεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ.
8:20.targetText: He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.

groups.note: ἐν ("in, at") is rendered near.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:21.sourceText: Εἶπεν οὖν πάλιν αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ ὑπάγω καὶ ζητήσετέ με, καὶ ἐν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ὑμῶν ἀποθανεῖσθε· ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν.
8:21.targetText: Again He said to them, “I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered but for the contrast.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:22.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Μήτι ἀποκτενεῖ ἑαυτὸν, ὅτι λέγει Ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν;
8:22.targetText: So the Jews began to ask, “Will He kill Himself, since He says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγον ("were saying") is rendered began to ask.

unmappedSource.reason: Μήτι only marks a question expecting the answer no; English has a plain question.

8:23.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐκ τῶν κάτω ἐστέ, ἐγὼ ἐκ τῶν ἄνω εἰμί· ὑμεῖς ἐκ τούτου τοῦ κόσμου ἐστέ, ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.
8:23.targetText: Then He told them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.

groups.note: τῶν κάτω ("the things below") is rendered below.
τῶν ἄνω ("the things above") is rendered above.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:24.sourceText: εἶπον οὖν ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀποθανεῖσθε ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν· ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πιστεύσητε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι, ἀποθανεῖσθε ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν.
8:24.targetText: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a predicate; ἐγώ εἰμι ("I am") has none.

8:25.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Σὺ τίς εἶ; εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τὴν ἀρχὴν ὅ τι καὶ λαλῶ ὑμῖν;
8:25.targetText: “Who are You?” they asked.  “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning,” Jesus replied.

groups.note: The accusative τὴν ἀρχήν is used as an adverb; BSB renders it from the beginning.
Same expression, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The intensive καί ("even, indeed") is rendered Just.

BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.

8:26.sourceText: πολλὰ ἔχω περὶ ὑμῶν λαλεῖν καὶ κρίνειν· ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με ἀληθής ἐστιν, κἀγὼ ἃ ἤκουσα παρ’ αὐτοῦ, ταῦτα λαλῶ εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
8:26.targetText: “I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.”

groups.note: πολλά is the object of both infinitives; BSB repeats much.
κἀγώ is καί + ἐγώ ("and I"); its I is the subject of tell.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive ταῦτα ("these things") repeats the object what, which English states once.
εἰς ("to") is absorbed in English tell the world.

8:27.sourceText: οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι τὸν Πατέρα αὐτοῖς ἔλεγεν.
8:27.targetText: They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.

8:28.sourceText: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὅταν ὑψώσητε τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, τότε γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ ποιῶ οὐδέν, ἀλλὰ καθὼς ἐδίδαξέν με ὁ Πατὴρ, ταῦτα λαλῶ.
8:28.targetText: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.

groups.note: BSB takes the following καί clause under the same ὅτι and repeats that.
καθὼς … ταῦτα ("just as … these things") is rendered exactly what.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a predicate; ἐγώ εἰμι ("I am") has none.

8:29.sourceText: καὶ ὁ πέμψας με μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν· οὐκ ἀφῆκέν με μόνον, ὅτι ἐγὼ τὰ ἀρεστὰ αὐτῷ ποιῶ πάντοτε.
8:29.targetText: He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.”

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not rendered.

8:30.sourceText: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν.
8:30.targetText: As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("he") is rendered Jesus.

8:31.sourceText: Ἔλεγεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς πεπιστευκότας αὐτῷ Ἰουδαίους Ἐὰν ὑμεῖς μείνητε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῷ ἐμῷ, ἀληθῶς μαθηταί μού ἐστε,
8:31.targetText: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.

groups.note: BSB says He for the name Jesus here.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:32.sourceText: καὶ γνώσεσθε τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια ἐλευθερώσει ὑμᾶς.
8:32.targetText: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

8:33.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν πρὸς αὐτόν Σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ ἐσμεν, καὶ οὐδενὶ δεδουλεύκαμεν πώποτε· πῶς σὺ λέγεις ὅτι Ἐλεύθεροι γενήσεσθε;
8:33.targetText: “We are Abraham’s descendants,” they answered. “We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?”

groups.note: οὐδενὶ … πώποτε ("to no one … ever") is rendered never … to anyone.
The second person γενήσεσθε ("you will become") is rendered we will be set, as reported speech.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to Him") unexpressed.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.
ὅτι introduces the content of what is said; English omits that.

8:34.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν δοῦλός ἐστιν τῆς ἁμαρτίας.

groups.note: ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ("the one who practices sin") is rendered who sins.
The genitive ("of sin") is rendered to sin.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι introduces the quoted words and has no English counterpart.

8:35.sourceText: ὁ δὲ δοῦλος οὐ μένει ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· ὁ υἱὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
8:35.targetText: A slave is not a permanent member of the family, but a son belongs to it forever.

groups.note: μένει ("remains") is rendered is; BSB recasts does not remain … forever as is not a permanent member.
ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ("in the household") is rendered a member of the family.
εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("forever") is rendered as the adjective permanent.
μένει ("remains") is rendered belongs to.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a contrast between the two clauses; the Greek joins them without a connective (the δέ opens the verse).
English refers back to the family; the Greek has no object here.

8:36.sourceText: ἐὰν οὖν ὁ Υἱὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλευθερώσῃ, ὄντως ἐλεύθεροι ἔσεσθε.
8:36.targetText: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.

8:37.sourceText: οἶδα ὅτι σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ ἐστε· ἀλλὰ ζητεῖτέ με ἀποκτεῖναι, ὅτι ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν.
8:37.targetText: I know you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.

groups.note: χωρεῖ means "makes room, finds a place".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:38.sourceText: ἃ ἐγὼ ἑώρακα παρὰ τῷ Πατρὶ λαλῶ· καὶ ὑμεῖς οὖν ἃ ἠκούσατε παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ποιεῖτε.
8:38.targetText: I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”

groups.note: The article serves as a possessive: your father.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.

8:39.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ τέκνα τοῦ Ἀβραάμ ἐστε, τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ποιεῖτε·
8:39.targetText: “Abraham is our father,” they replied.  “If you were children of Abraham,” said Jesus, “you would do the works of Abraham.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.
Same verb; BSB's Greek has another form of it here, rendered would do (N1904's present means "you do" or "do").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

8:40.sourceText: νῦν δὲ ζητεῖτέ με ἀποκτεῖναι, ἄνθρωπον ὃς τὴν ἀλήθειαν ὑμῖν λελάληκα, ἣν ἤκουσα παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ· τοῦτο Ἀβραὰμ οὐκ ἐποίησεν.
8:40.targetText: But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.

groups.note: The first-person λελάληκα ("I have told") is rendered has told after a man who.
τοῦτο ("this") is rendered such a thing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:41.sourceText: ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν. εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἡμεῖς ἐκ πορνείας οὐκ ἐγεννήθημεν, ἕνα Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Θεόν.
8:41.targetText: You are doing the works of your father.”  “We are not illegitimate children,” they declared. “Our only Father is God Himself.”

groups.note: ἐκ πορνείας ἐγεννήθημεν ("we were born of sexual immorality") is rendered are … illegitimate children.
ἕνα ("one") is rendered only.
ἔχομεν ("we have") is recast as Our … is.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
Greek states to Him with the reply; BSB leaves that recipient implicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds intensive Himself with God; no independent intensive pronoun is printed in this N1904 verse.

8:42.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ ὁ Θεὸς Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἦν, ἠγαπᾶτε ἂν ἐμέ· ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἥκω· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ ἐλήλυθα, ἀλλ’ ἐκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν.
8:42.targetText: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.

groups.note: ἥκω means "I have come, I am here".

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins ἐξῆλθον and ἥκω into one clause and does not render καί.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering γάρ.

8:43.sourceText: διὰ τί τὴν λαλιὰν τὴν ἐμὴν οὐ γινώσκετε; ὅτι οὐ δύνασθε ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐμόν.
8:43.targetText: Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.

groups.note: λαλιά ("speech, way of speaking") is rendered what I am saying.
The possessive ἐμήν ("my") becomes the subject I.
ἀκούειν ("to hear") is rendered to accept.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb before because; the Greek has ὅτι alone.

8:44.sourceText: ὑμεῖς ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστὲ καὶ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν θέλετε ποιεῖν. ἐκεῖνος ἀνθρωποκτόνος ἦν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ οὐκ ἔστηκεν, ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν αὐτῷ. ὅταν λαλῇ τὸ ψεῦδος, ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων λαλεῖ, ὅτι ψεύστης ἐστὶν καὶ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ.
8:44.targetText: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.

groups.note: ἐκ … ἐστέ ("you are of") is rendered belong to.
The article serves as a possessive: your father.
τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν ("of your father") is rendered his.
οὐκ ἔστηκεν ("does not stand") is rendered refusing to uphold.
λαλῇ τὸ ψεῦδος ("he speaks the lie") is rendered he lies.
ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων ("from his own") is rendered his native language.
αὐτοῦ ("of it" or "of him") is rendered of lies.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns this clause into the participle phrase refusing … instead of rendering καί.
ἐν ("in") is absorbed in English uphold the truth.

8:45.sourceText: ἐγὼ δὲ ὅτι τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω, οὐ πιστεύετέ μοι.
8:45.targetText: But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!

8:46.sourceText: τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐλέγχει με περὶ ἁμαρτίας; εἰ ἀλήθειαν λέγω, διὰ τί ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετέ μοι;
8:46.targetText: Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?

8:47.sourceText: ὁ ὢν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀκούει· διὰ τοῦτο ὑμεῖς οὐκ ἀκούετε, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἐστέ.
8:47.targetText: Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.”

groups.note: ὁ ὢν ἐκ ("the one who is of") is rendered Whoever belongs to.
διὰ τοῦτο … ὅτι ("for this reason … because") is rendered The reason … is that.
ἐκ … ἐστέ ("you are of") is rendered belong to.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:48.sourceText: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Οὐ καλῶς λέγομεν ἡμεῖς ὅτι Σαμαρείτης εἶ σὺ καὶ δαιμόνιον ἔχεις;
8:48.targetText: The Jews answered Him, “Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?”

groups.note: Ἀπεκρίθησαν … καὶ εἶπαν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb answered.
The adverb καλῶς ("rightly") is rendered right.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedTarget.reason: English recasts Οὐ καλῶς λέγομεν ("Do we not say rightly") as Are we not right to say.

8:49.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἐγὼ δαιμόνιον οὐκ ἔχω, ἀλλὰ τιμῶ τὸν Πατέρα μου, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀτιμάζετέ με.
8:49.targetText: “I do not have a demon,” Jesus replied, “but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:50.sourceText: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ ζητῶ τὴν δόξαν μου· ἔστιν ὁ ζητῶν καὶ κρίνων.
8:50.targetText: I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.

groups.note: The participle κρίνων ("judging"), under the same article as ζητῶν, is rendered He is the Judge.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds own for emphasis; the Greek has only μου ("my").
English supplies the object; ζητῶν has none.
English recasts the participle as a new clause.

8:51.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐάν τις τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον τηρήσῃ, θάνατον οὐ μὴ θεωρήσῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
8:51.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”

groups.note: οὐ μή … εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("not ever … forever") is rendered never.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:52.sourceText: εἶπαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Νῦν ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι δαιμόνιον ἔχεις. Ἀβραὰμ ἀπέθανεν καὶ οἱ προφῆται, καὶ σὺ λέγεις Ἐάν τις τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσῃ, οὐ μὴ γεύσηται θανάτου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
8:52.targetText: “Now we know that You have a demon!” declared the Jews. “Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.

groups.note: Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text.
BSB repeats the verb as so did with the prophets.
Ἐάν τις ("if anyone") is rendered anyone who.
μου ("My") is rendered Your in reported speech.
οὐ μή … εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("not ever … forever") is rendered never.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies that; the Greek quotes the words directly.

8:53.sourceText: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ, ὅστις ἀπέθανεν; καὶ οἱ προφῆται ἀπέθανον· τίνα σεαυτὸν ποιεῖς;
8:53.targetText: Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?”

groups.note: The relative ὅστις ("who") starts a new sentence in English: He died.
καί ("and") is rendered as.
ἀπέθανον ("died") is rendered by did, standing for died.
σεαυτὸν ποιεῖς ("You make Yourself") is rendered do You claim to be.

unmappedSource.reason: μή only marks a question expecting the answer no; English has a plain question.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:54.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἐὰν ἐγὼ δοξάσω ἐμαυτόν, ἡ δόξα μου οὐδέν ἐστιν· ἔστιν ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ δοξάζων με, ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐστιν,
8:54.targetText: Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say ‘He is our God.’

groups.note: ἐστιν ("is") is rendered means.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι introduces the quoted words and has no English counterpart.

8:55.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἐγνώκατε αὐτόν, ἐγὼ δὲ οἶδα αὐτόν. κἂν εἴπω ὅτι οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν, ἔσομαι ὅμοιος ὑμῖν ψεύστης· ἀλλὰ οἶδα αὐτὸν καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ τηρῶ.
8:55.targetText: You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not rendered.
BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

8:56.sourceText: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἠγαλλιάσατο ἵνα ἴδῃ τὴν ἡμέραν τὴν ἐμήν, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐχάρη.
8:56.targetText: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; εἶδεν has none.

8:57.sourceText: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν Πεντήκοντα ἔτη οὔπω ἔχεις καὶ Ἀβραὰμ ἑώρακας;
8:57.targetText: Then the Jews said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?”

groups.note: Same verb, in another form in BSB's Greek text.
ἔχεις ("You have") fifty years is rendered You are … years old.

8:58.sourceText: εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ γενέσθαι ἐγὼ εἰμί.
8:58.targetText: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am!”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.

8:59.sourceText: ἦραν οὖν λίθους ἵνα βάλωσιν ἐπ’ αὐτόν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐκρύβη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ.
8:59.targetText: At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.
